changes_summary: GroundCombatScreen.ts exists with three phases: planning (troop slider + launch/cancel), resolving (animated combat rounds with dice rolls and troop bars), and result (victory/defeat/pyrrhic screens). The implementation structure follows the design doc well. However, critical bugs were found in the resolving phase casualty display and missing population status on result screens.
blocking_issues: RESOLVING PHASE BUG: Line ~398 in casualties panel uses round.casualties (same value) for both attacker AND defender lost counts. Should show attacker casualties vs defender casualties separately.
RESULT PHASE: Missing planetary status section that design specifies — surviving population, factories intact, missile bases cleared. Shows casualties but not planet condition.
PLANETARY STATUS: Design doc requires showing population changes on result screen (surviving population transferred, factories destroyed, etc.), but UI only shows troop loss numbers.
notes:
STRUCTURE: Well-organized three-phase UI matching design. Planning, resolving, and result phases all implemented. Speed controls present (Slow/Normal/Fast/Instant) but as buttons instead of radio buttons. Combat simulation uses simulateGroundCombat from groundCombat.ts correctly. Troop bars with color-coded health states implemented.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. Attacker troops & bonuses: ✅ Displayed correctly with bonus calculation
2. Defender population & bonuses: ⚠️ Shows 'Troops' not 'Population' — minor terminology mismatch
3. Combat rounds with casualties: ⚠️ Shows rounds but casualty bug (same value for both sides)
4. Final result (captured/failed): ✅ Victory, defeat, pyrrhic all handled
5. Population changes: ❌ Missing planetary status section entirely
6. Return to galaxy map: ✅ dispatches NAVIGATE to 'galaxy' screen

TEST COVERAGE: Only groundCombat.test.ts exists (35 tests) covering the game system layer (calculateGroundCombatOdds, executeGroundCombat, transferTroops, capturePlanet). NO tests exist for GroundCombatScreen UI component. UI tests should cover: planning phase rendering, slider interaction, launchInvasion triggering, round advancement, speed control switching, result phase rendering for all three outcomes.

NON-BLOCKING ISSUES:
- Speed controls use button group instead of radio buttons per design
- Troop bar has 3 color levels (green/yellow/red) vs design's 4
- Enslave button lacks race-trait gating (design notes it's conditional)
- Pyrrhic victory detection uses 0.7 threshold (not explicitly specified in design)
